newsitem.title: CHINA: "Unnecessary" to tighten HK mortgage lending -HKMA.
newsitem.headline: "Unnecessary" to tighten HK mortgage lending -HKMA.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Monday a tightening in mortgage lending seemed unncessary given recent cooling in the territory's property market, but it did not rule out future action.
"At present, further tightening does not seem necessary, though it is not ruled out for the future," HKMA deputy chief executive David Carse said in a statement.
"The market has cooled recently in light of the government's intention to increase the supply of residential property and to deal resolutely with sopeculation," he said.
Carse said lending institutions should strictly apply existing criteria, including those on loan-to-value ratios, "top up" loans, and debt servicing ratios.

"To this end, we have issued a letter to all authorised institutions reminding them of key aspects of such criteria and the fact that the HKMA will take a serious view if institutions are not compliant," he said.

The HKMA also said its monthly survey showed gross new loans decreased in June by two percent to HK$25.5 billion from the month before, while the average size of new loans shrank to HK$1.88 million from HK$1.91 million in May.
New loans approved in June rose by 4.8 percent to HK$31.5 billion and new loans approved but not yet drawn rose to a record level of HK$20.4 billion.
The price-cutting trend continued, the HKMA said, with 31.8 percent of new loans approved in June being priced at the best lending rate, compared with 18 percent in May.
The amount of loans granted at 0.25 percent above the best rate fell to 46.9 percent from 56.7 percent in May.
Repayment of loans dropped in June, the HKMA said. The amount of outstanding loans increased 2.7 percent to HK$379.6 billion, the same as the growth in May, it said.
